title: Domain and Metadata Semantics
current_summary: Current focus is the accepted domain/meta bridge-DSL reset: Functional Model requirements are the source for a smaller shared meta language between domain and IO, with adapter preservation and targeted deletion of historical sediment. The Domain Maintainer Contract is now canonical; its first pilot confirmed FK Relation Helpers and Lookup Enrichment as separate semantic owners, and that pilot's Family Cycle 1 (remove remaining ontology) has since closed too (see CONC-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS / SIG-ACT-FK-FAMILY-CYCLE1-CLOSED).
next_action: Create contract-backed FTR slices that derive bridge DSL portions from Functional Model use cases; do not golden-master current implementation workarounds. FTR-FK-REFERENCE-HELPER-SURFACE-CONSOLIDATION-P5 (choosing one canonical public helper-column surface between add_fk_helpers and add_lookup_helpers) remains queued, not started, and explicitly UNDECIDED. It is no longer gated on the Domain Maintainer Contract's existence -- DMC is canonical, and its first pilot (the FK/reference-helper family) is complete through Family Cycle 1. That pilot's independent review (Cycle-0 finding F-004) distinguished this FTR's 'public surface consolidation' question from the separate 'semantic ownership merger' question the pilot answered; do not treat the pilot, or its Family Cycle 1 closure, as having resolved or replaced this FTR -- no add_fk_helpers/add_lookup_helpers, one-verb, common-mechanism, or migration decision is made. Do not broaden Trusted Ingress certification to the legacy add_fk_helpers formula producer as a substitute.
notes: This concern is a steering field, not a replacement for FTRs or concrete finding tracking. ADR-CONTRACT-FIRST-DOMAIN-META-REWRITE records the counter-conservative direction: low adoption makes breaking domain/meta changes acceptable when they reduce sediment and stabilize the bridge DSL.

title: Adapter and Spreadsheet Boundary
current_summary: Spreadsheet assurance has distinct open surfaces: read-side parser expansion, resource, filesystem, and metadata costs precede Trusted Ingress, while write-side formula activation, serializability, and persistence behavior belong to sink/backend boundaries.
next_action: Keep H1/H2 under the existing XLSX parser/resource-limit FTR and sequence any H3-H5 or IOR-01/02 corrections through explicit bounded work; do not claim public hostile-input readiness from semantic ingress alone.
notes: The September hostile-input and IO reviews are non-authorizing evidence. Parser hardening, Trusted Ingress conformance, controlled-role authorization, and sink durability are complementary boundaries rather than one security mechanism.

title: User Surface and Adoption
current_summary: A maintained consumer proved configured Workbook View names and ordering across XLSX and ODS reimport, and the User Guide now documents the generic forward and inbound workflow; no missing capability surfaced. Grouped-XRef exact workbook projection is now also publicly reachable through a configured Workbook View and the router XLSX/ODS save paths (FTR-XREF-AXIS-MAPPINGS-P4A2 GX-5, accepted and Done).
next_action: Review after the next public-surface or release-preparation slice rather than turning every low-priority doc signal into a task.
notes: REVIEW-003 made this visible as a real concern thread, but it is not the current highest-pressure implementation slice.

title: Projection Ergonomics
current_summary: Dynamic column-axis crosstable projection now has an accepted baseline: axis mappings resolve live from source frames and are never persisted, flat and grouped axis-label projections compose around unchanged XRef over canonical string identity, and the grouped multi-row header roundtrips through XLSX and ODS via the backend-neutral core.ExactTable carrier. GX-5 public adoption is now accepted: grouped-XRef exact workbook projection is reachable through a configured Workbook View and the router XLSX/ODS save paths, so the FTR is Done. Remaining projection pressure is limited to later dynamic-view, discriminator-multiprojection, or editing gaps.
next_action: Keep further projection work tied to concrete dynamic-view, discriminator-multiprojection, or editing gaps; grouped-XRef adoption is complete and needs no follow-up FTR.
notes: Active as a strategic pressure field, but many concrete changes should wait for domain/meta clarification.

title: Backend Portability
current_summary: The shared RenderPlan architecture remains viable for XLSX and ODS; current portability risk is concentrated at formula activation, sink serializability/durability, directory overlay behavior, and cross-backend semantic differences.
next_action: Preserve the shared plan/parity architecture while addressing only evidence-backed sink-boundary gaps; keep IOR-01 through IOR-03 visible and retain IOR-04 as resolved historical evidence.
notes: IOR-04 is closed: capability truth is router-owned, translated at the application composition seam, and passed into backend-neutral execution state. No renderer rewrite or general transactional output layer is justified by the review.

title: Maintainability Hygiene
current_summary: Maintainability and local readability are judged through bounded reconstruction inside sound architecture, not mechanical cleanup. Module size, package surfaces, and module headers are inspection signals, not findings by themselves: split or add structure only on concrete responsibility, ownership, unstable-package-surface, reconstruction, or validation-locality evidence, and preserve cohesive long operations where extraction would increase non-local reasoning. The three-family Human Readability investigation validated this (XRef operation.py ~516 LOC and dense_axes.py ~411 LOC are cohesive and locally reconstructable).
next_action: Apply the bounded-reconstruction questions in ordinary reviews; open implementation only on concrete reader/ownership cost plus explicit authority. Add module headers where they give real orientation, not as a uniform mandate; do not run a mechanical cleanup wave. A Human Readability Guide or Sentinel experiment requires separate authorization.
notes: Many low/medium findings are heatmap signals for this concern rather than individual tasks. Reconciled 2026-08-04 with the three-family Human Readability evidence (REVSET-TOPIC-HUMAN-READABILITY, DEC-HUMAN-READABILITY-BOUNDED-RECONSTRUCTION): LOC alone is not a finding, and the module-size/modularization/header FTR records (FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULARIZATION-P4A, FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULE-HEADERS-P5, FTR-MAINTAINER-ENTRYPOINTS-AND-MODULE-BUDGETS-P5) were narrowed accordingly. Real package-surface, ownership, unrelated-responsibility, and agent read-window concerns remain valid.

title: Pipeline YAML Contract vs Callable Signature
current_summary: TODO -- clarify and enforce the boundary among callable signatures, generic binder-reserved fields, BoundStep metadata, and the public YAML step contract. registries/pipeline_step_registry.json mirrors callable parameters, but reserved YAML fields such as name may not reach the callable: the generic binders in pipeline/steps.py (make_builder_target_step, make_frames_target_step) reserve name for the BoundStep label and do not forward it inside **kwargs. Concretely, the Compact Multiaxis callable exposes name: str | None to set its own stable config_id, but YAML authors cannot currently reach that parameter through YAML name; expand/contract fall back to deriving config_id from output/relation.
next_action: Decide whether the registry needs separate callable and YAML parameter surfaces, explicit binder metadata, validation, or a namespaced callable config ID. The immediate Compact Multiaxis symptom (stale diagnostics trace IDs surviving a frame rename) is owned by FTR-COMPACT-MULTIAXIS-TRACE-LIFECYCLE-COMMANDS-P5; this concern tracks the broader registry/binder contract question, which is not scoped to any single FTR yet.
notes: Raised while implementing the Compact Multiaxis meta-persistence-correction and trace-lifecycle FTRs; verified directly against pipeline/build.py and pipeline/steps.py, not inferred from documentation alone. Evidence anchored by SIG-ACT-PIPELINE-YAML-CALLABLE-CONTRACT-TODO.

title: Project Memory Governance
current_summary: Project Memory must remain a reliable locator over durable evidence and an aggressively compressed steering layer, with canonical JSON curated deliberately and Cold Storage separated from active working context.
next_action: Curate only after meaningful review or implementation waves: keep review/FTR/finding locators aligned with actual Cold topology, regenerate rebuildable projections, and reject per-commit or automatically promoted candidate memory.
notes: Governance covers canonical granularity, review indexing, locator consistency, bounded curation, and rebuildable workbook/derived projections. Workflow Coordinator product architecture has its own concern.

title: Domain Boundary Robustness
current_summary: Trusted Ingress remains the accepted semantic post-parse boundary, while FK/reference-helper Cycle 3 is active and partial: C3-S1 is complete, C3-S2 is assessed ready but not authorized, and broader identity/assurance questions remain open.
next_action: Require separate authority before C3-S2 or any remaining Cycle-3 slice, and assess the September post-state assurance findings as proposals without treating universal re-establishment or certification simplification as adopted design.
notes: DMC is canonical and earlier FK family cycles remain closed. Current evidence distinguishes semantic admission, actual post-state assurance, and parser/resource boundaries; detailed E1-E7 and FK chronology remains in prior events, FTRs, reviews, and Cold Storage.

title: Workflow Coordinator Authority, Evidence, and Product Boundary
current_summary: The Coordinator has proven bounded serial execution and one real Useful Loop, while governing-input authority, evidence sufficiency, reachable trust/egress surfaces, and a truthful future product boundary remain the long-lived strategic field.
next_action: Use separately authorized work to close concrete authority and evidence gaps before routine live use or carve-out; keep review proposals non-normative until accepted and preserve consumer versus Coordinator ownership at any future lifecycle boundary.
notes: One concern covers Slice 5A/5B proofs, W7 commissioning learning, outer-loop authority, professional trust, and carve-out evidence. Detailed findings stay in reviews/findings/FTR/Git rather than becoming separate concerns.
